messages:
Jenna (Sales): Priya from Acme flagged issues during POC onboarding — users can SSO into Console but they can't see Dedicated pool resources or switch teams.
Priya (Acme IT): We can log into Console via SAML but when trying to access the Dedicated namespace we get 403 Forbidden 'not authorized'. SCIM shows users created but roles empty.
Sam (Solutions Eng): That sounds like role mapping isn't coming through from SCIM. Azure's auto-provisioning creates users but unless the group/entitlements attribute maps to our 'roles' extension, Console won't grant team access.
Priya (Acme IT): In Azure provisioning mappings we only mapped basic fields. What's the expected group/role attribute schema?
Sam (Solutions Eng): We expect an extension attribute: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:roles or groups -> members. For Azure AD, set the mapping: groupMembershipClaims -> "SecurityGroup" and then map `memberOf` or use a custom app attribute that exports group names.
Marco (SRE): Also check Dedicated side — if the user is part of multiple org domains we enforce allowed_domains and team membership tag. If SCIM creates the user without email or role, our RBAC layer denies Dedicated resources.
Priya (Acme IT): SCIM provisioning log snippet:
```
POST /scim/v2/Users
201 Created
Payload: {"userName":"j.priya@acme.co.uk","emails":[],"urn:extension:roles": []}
```
Priya (Acme IT): Emails array empty — we never mapped userPrincipalName -> emails[0].value because we followed Microsoft quickstart.
Sam (Solutions Eng): Two fixes — edit Azure mapping so user.userPrincipalName -> emails[0].value or change our allowed_domains to accept acme.co.uk for POC. And map group claims to urn:extension:roles.
Priya (Acme IT): Any risks to relaxing allowed_domains? We only want POC users.
Kai (Security): For POC we can temporarily allow acme.co.uk but scope it to the provisioning token. Also ensure SCIM token has least privilege and rotate after POC. Ask Sam to issue a short-lived token.
Jenna (Sales): Customer also asked if they can use Hosted API keys for the demo while SCIM is fixed.
Sam (Solutions Eng): Yes — Hosted API keys are independent. Create an API key in Console -> API Keys, choose 'demo' policy to cap usage. Note: keys don't map to Console users and won't grant Dedicated pool access.
Priya (Acme IT): Could we use a CLI to verify user roles once SCIM runs? A quick endpoint to list user objects?
Sam (Solutions Eng): Yes. Use our SCIM GET and our admin user listing endpoint. Example:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <<SCIM_TOKEN>>" https://console.redwood.ai/scim/v2/Users | jq '.Resources[] | {userName: .userName, emails: .emails, roles: .urn:extension:roles}'
```
Marco (SRE): Also if you hit the dedicated API and see 403, capture the X-Request-ID header and paste it here. We'll trace across the RBAC service.
Priya (Acme IT): Ran the curl after remapping userPrincipalName -> emails[0].value and mapping groups -> urn:extension:roles. Now GET returns roles populated.
idp-bot: Provisioning run #7 10 users created/updated, roles assigned for 8 users.
Priya (Acme IT): Confirmed a user can switch to Dedicated namespace and list pools.
Jenna (Sales): Great. Action items:
- Sam: create 7-day SCIM token and a limited Hosted API key (demo policy); DM to Priya. Provide sample mapping YAML and curl snippets for the docs.
- Marco: temporarily allow acme.co.uk for POC in allowed_domains and record the change in the ticket.
- Kai: send token rotation and risk note to Priya.
- Priya: confirm demo accounts and try Dedicated operations end-to-end.
Sam (Solutions Eng): Will do. Also adding a note: Azure sometimes base64-encodes role lists in group claims. If you see an encoded string, decode it before mapping.
Jenna (Sales): I'll update the CRM and mark onboarding unblocked for the demo. Thanks everyone.
